A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DLBS and reward-calibration research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original reward-calibration experiments, search comparisons, ablations, VLM evaluations, and sample-diversity results using Latte.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds human evaluations, additional model and dataset results, estimator analyses, and image-generation experiments.

M1.justification: The original DDIM beam-search and lookahead algorithms remain unchanged. V2 adds an adaptation using SDE-DPMSolver++ for beam search and deterministic DPMSolver++ for lookahead with Wan 2.1 (Appendix D, Algorithms 3–4).

E1.justification: V2 retains MSRVTT-test and DEVIL high/medium/static coverage, while adding more challenging DEVIL-very-high and MovieGen prompts. It also evaluates VLM agreement with human labels on TVGE and extends evaluation to text-to-image generation across 45 animal categories.

E2.justification: Best-of-N and greedy search remain the principal baselines. V2 adds an evaluated FK Steering comparator on MSRVTT-test (Appendix L.8, Figure 25); its underlying work was cited but not experimentally compared in v1.

E3.justification: V2 introduces evaluation against NFE and wall-clock cost, VideoScore assessment at 8 fps, three-rater pairwise human comparisons, and additional model-size and generation configurations. It expands lookahead/search settings and evaluates all 1,003 MovieGen prompts. Sections 4–5 also change reward reporting from weighted sums to weight-normalized combinations and state min/max normalization.

E4.justification: V2 adds reward-estimation error measurements and a 20-step lookahead saturation test (Appendix L.4), tests VLM–human agreement on TVGE (Appendix J), and extends diversity analysis to DLBS-LA (Appendix L.7). Existing denoising-window, DDIM-noise, and shorter-lookahead ablations are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report Pearson correlations with p-values, and v2 extends that same practice to additional analyses. Its checklist clarifies averaging rewards across prompts but introduces no changed uncertainty procedure. Neither version specifies repeated-run/seed counts or defined uncertainty intervals for the main search comparisons.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive human, VideoScore, TVGE, larger-model, and image-generation results. Its new MovieGen experiment reports 0.3243 for GS and 0.3918 for DLBS-LA (Figure 8). Existing results also change: GS has greater MSRVTT-test ViCLIP diversity than DLBS in v2 Figure 24, reversing v1 Figure 10's ordering. Rescaled reward values should not themselves be interpreted as cross-version performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated lookahead convergence argument using assumed solver error rates, the Continuous Mapping Theorem, and a Lipschitz reward-error bound (Appendix E). V1 contains the stochastic-control motivation and practical approximations but no corresponding analysis of lookahead convergence.

C1.justification: V2 expands the central claims to human-assessed quality and applicability across multiple capable generative models. Its abstract, introduction, and conclusion emphasize computational efficiency under comparable costs, extending v1's emphasis on calibrated/VLM rewards and search-budget scaling.

C2.justification: V2 interprets longer-lookahead results as saturation around six steps, attributes FK Steering's weakness to infrequent resampling, and uses TVGE correlations to argue that VLM optimization tracks human preference. The central qualifications concerning VLM proxies and computational cost remain.

D1.justification: V1 documents Latte configuration, hardware, checkpoints, and timing. V2 adds project implementation links and model-specific scheduler, guidance, frame-count, resolution, precision, and GPU details for CogVideoX and Wan 2.1 (Appendix B). These substantially broaden reproducibility information without establishing changes to the retained Latte setup.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for CogVideoX, Wan, MovieGen, PixArt-alpha, DPMSolver++, and solver-convergence analysis. The main positioning relative to guidance, SMC, and finetuning remains largely unchanged, with an additional empirical discussion of the already-cited FK Steering work.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative and appendices are substantially reorganized. Earlier diffusion-step and diversity subsections move into Appendix L, while the main text foregrounds computational cost, human evaluation, and model scaling. Prose is edited throughout, implementation details gain subsections, and a conference checklist is appended.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text from two columns to one and extensively recomposes figures. Figure 1 gains a timing panel; correlation and scaling grids are split between main text and appendices; qualitative panels are reduced or revised; and human, model-scaling, estimator-error, and image-generation displays are added. V1's timing table is replaced by graphical cost reporting.

improvement.justification: V1's evidence relies on Latte, limited prompt coverage, and VLM-based assessment. V2 materially strengthens validation through direct human preferences, independent VideoScore and TVGE evaluations, challenging prompts, additional backbones, and explicit compute comparisons (Sections 5.1–5.4; Appendices J and L). These address important gaps in generality and perceptual-quality evidence. Human-study detail and uncertainty reporting remain limited, and the revised diversity plots do not uniformly support superiority, but the overall evidential improvement is substantial.
